title: Sales enablement playbook - positioning, messaging, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Liam Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference core positioning and messaging, short competitive battlecards, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance for discovery conversations, case study templates, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical go-to-market reference for outbound, AE enablement, and pre-sales engineering handoffs.

Intended audience
- Account Executives
- Solutions Engineers
- Sales Engineers and Pre-sales
- Customer Success in trial/POC handoff
- Product marketing and field marketing

1) Positioning and core messaging

One-line value proposition
- Redwood Inference: predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Core pillars (use as headers in one-pagers and slide decks)
- Production-first performance: predictable latency and throughput for user-facing applications.
- Unified developer experience: same API, SDKs, and rollouts across hosted, dedicated, and private.
- Cost-aware controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization guidance to reduce unit economics.
- Enterprise-grade operations: observability, model rollouts, and policy-based routing to meet SLAs.

Persona-focused messaging
- Product and platform engineers: emphasis on predictable throughput, autoscaling, and per-route performance breakdowns in Redwood Console.
- ML engineers: focus on model variant support, quantization profiles, and regression monitoring tied to evals.
- Security and infra owners: highlight VPC/private control plane, KMS integration, audit logs, and optional on-prem packaging.

Key proof points to use in conversation
- Verified performance profiles for curated open models.
- Example: customer X moved from a 450ms median latency to 150ms after enabling Dedicated pools and KV caching.
- Integrated rollouts: canary and automatic fallback policies that reduce operational risk during model upgrades.

2) Competitive brief (one-page battlecard)

Competitors covered (short list)
- Large hosted LLM APIs (market leaders)
- Safety-focused model providers (Anthropic-style)
- Self-hosted inference vendors and managed GPU marketplaces

Differentiators vs hosted LLM APIs
- Multi-mode deployment: hosted API plus Dedicated and Private options for isolation and compliance.
- Better unit-cost levers via automatic batching and intelligent caching.
- Transparent performance profiles and per-route observability.

Differentiators vs safety-focused model providers
- Comparable safety tooling but stronger operational controls and deployment flexibility (VPC, on-prem).
- Easier integration with existing infra and KMS/HSM.

Differentiators vs self-hosted inference vendors
- Less operational burden: Redwood provides a unified control plane, verified kernel selection, and managed autoscaling.
- Faster time-to-production with SDKs, templates, and prebuilt rollouts.

Objection handling (short scripts)
- Objection: we can self-host and save money. Response: for scale, the hidden costs are ops headcount, regression risk, and model tuning. We provide predictable economics and tooling that often lowers TCO when factoring reliability and developer time.
- Objection: we need data residency. Response: Redwood Private provides on-prem and VPC deployments with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; share the private deployment checklist.

3) Pitch deck outline and talk track

Recommended slide flow (10-12 slides)
1. Title & 30-second value prop
2. Customer pain: unpredictable latency, cost surprises, and model regressions
3. Solution overview: Redwood product surface (Redwood API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize)
4. Architecture diagram: smart routing, caching, and deployment abstraction (one-slide sketch)
5. Performance & cost proof points: verified model profiles and before/after customer metrics
6. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, SOC2/ISO mentions, audit logging
7. Pricing summary & deployment options (high level)
8. Customer success stories / logos (case studies)
9. Implementation plan and timelines for POC to production
10. TCO comparison versus 3rd-party options
11. Next steps and trial/POC offer
12. Appendix: detailed SLOs, integration checklist, sample API calls

Demo script (6 minutes recommended for discovery calls)
1. Quick assertive statement of value and POC objective (30s).
2. Live API demo generating a sample prompt; show streaming output (2m).
3. Console walkthrough: per-route latency, cost breakdown, and rollout config (2m).
4. Show model variant switch and automatic fallback (30s).
5. Close with POC next steps and ask for infra/security contacts (30s).

4) Pricing guidance for discovery conversations

High level pricing constructs to present
- Hosted API: usage-based metering for generation, chat, and embeddings. Offer developer free tier and usage credits for new accounts.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with monthly or annual commits for predictable throughput and isolation. Includes autoscaling policies and burst capacity options.
- Private: license or subscription fee plus implementation and optional annual support. Includes on-prem packaging and private control plane.

Guidance for quoting and objection handling
- Use usage examples not raw rates: e.g., show a 100k monthly active users workload with average 150 tokens per interaction and compare hosted cost vs dedicated baseline.
- For enterprise customers, lead with Dedicated for SLO guarantees; offer a blended migration path: start with Hosted API, then transition to Dedicated as load grows.

Example pricing reference (illustrative only; confirm with pricing team)
| Deployment | Billing model | Typical starting point |
| Hosted API | per-token / per-embedding | sandbox/free to low-volume tier; scales with usage |
| Dedicated | monthly reserved capacity | typical starting commitment $25k/month for production-grade pool |
| Private | license + implementation + support | license + setup, variable based on footprint |

Negotiation levers
- Longer commitments for Dedicated lower unit cost.
- Pilot credits and extended evaluation windows for strategic accounts.
- Managed onboarding and extended support as paid add-ons.

5) Case study template and examples

Customer case study template (fill for closed deals)
- Customer name (industry)
- Situation: initial architecture and pain points
- Approach: config used (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), features enabled (KV caching, batching, quantization profile)
- Implementation timeline: discovery -> POC -> rollout
- Outcome: numeric results (latency P50/P95, cost per 1k requests, error reduction, business KPIs)
- Quote from customer contact
- Relevant assets: dashboards, screenshots, before/after charts

Example (fictionalized)
- Acme Retail (SaaS commerce)
- Situation: inconsistent inference latency causing cart abandonment and high cost per session.
- Approach: moved from hoster A to Redwood Dedicated, enabled prefix-KV caching and tuned batch sizes.
- Outcome: median latency reduced from 450ms to 150ms, P95 improved from 1.2s to 320ms, and per-interaction inference cost reduced by 42%.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (short, copy-ready answers)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: Hosted API: regional data residency controls per account; Dedicated and Private provide customer isolation and the option to deploy within a customer VPC or on-prem for full data residency.

Q: How is data encrypted?
A: All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest. Customers can opt for customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Q: What compliance evidence do you provide?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness artifacts. For enterprise customers we run security questionnaires, provide evidence under an NDA, and support audits for Private deployments.

Q: Can I run the control plane in my network?
A: Yes. Private deployment includes an option to host the control plane in customer-managed environments; engage eng-private-deployments for the checklist and timeline.

Q: How are logs and audit trails handled?
A: Audit logging is available across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Logs can be routed to customer SIEMs via secure forwarding; retention policies configurable by plan.

Q: How do you handle model and output safety?
A: We provide safety tooling for prompt filters, model-level guardrails, and regression monitoring via Redwood Optimize. For regulated workloads, combine Private deployment and eval-driven quality gates.
